toolLabs.title: Python: Load and Clean the Sample Dataset
toolLabs.brief: The chain starts here: load the fictional ecom_orders CSV in pandas, profile it, clean it (types, nulls, dedupe), and save a cleaned Parquet that every later lab builds on. This cleaned file is the single source of truth for the whole chain.
steps: Create the project folder il26-tool-chain/ and save the ecom_orders dataset as data/raw/ecom_orders.csv
Write clean_orders.py: read the CSV with pandas, print shape, dtypes, and null counts per column
Convert order_date to datetime, amount to numeric; strip whitespace and uppercase region/channel/category values
Deduplicate on order_id (keep first, log how many duplicates were found — expect zero, prove it)
Treat empty discount_code as 'NONE'; assert no negative amounts and no null order_ids (raise if violated)
Write the result to data/clean/ecom_orders_clean.parquet; print final row count and a 5-row sample
Commit clean_orders.py and the row-count log to git with message 'TL-01: cleaned orders baseline'
toolLabs.deliverable: data/clean/ecom_orders_clean.parquet plus clean_orders.py committed to git
toolLabs.checkpoint: Re-running clean_orders.py produces the identical Parquet (same row count, same checksum); the script raises loudly on any failed assertion instead of silently passing bad data.

toolLabs.title: SQL: Model It in DuckDB
toolLabs.brief: Move the cleaning logic from Python into SQL: create a persistent DuckDB database, define typed tables with constraints, and re-implement TL-01's cleaning as SQL transformations — the same dataset, now modeled the analytics-engineering way.
steps: Create analytics.duckdb and a raw schema: CREATE TABLE raw.orders AS FROM read_csv('data/raw/ecom_orders.csv', header=true)
Run data-quality checks in SQL: SELECT COUNT(*), COUNT(DISTINCT order_id), COUNT(amount) — record the baseline numbers
CREATE TABLE clean.orders AS SELECT with explicit CASTs: order_date::DATE, amount::DECIMAL(10,2), UPPER(TRIM(region))
Implement the TL-01 rules in SQL: COALESCE(NULLIF(discount_code,''), 'NONE'), dedupe with ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY order_id)
Add a date dimension table clean.dim_date (date, year, month, quarter, day_of_week) generated with generate_series
Build clean.orders_daily: one row per date with orders, revenue, avg_order — the mart the BI labs will consume
Verify parity: the DuckDB clean.orders row count and revenue total EXACTLY match the TL-01 Parquet (document both numbers)
toolLabs.deliverable: analytics.duckdb with raw.orders, clean.orders, clean.dim_date, clean.orders_daily, plus parity numbers vs TL-01
toolLabs.checkpoint: SELECT COUNT(*) and SUM(amount) from clean.orders match the TL-01 Parquet totals exactly; clean.orders_daily has one row per date with no gaps.

toolLabs.title: dbt: Models, Tests, and Docs from the SQL Layer
toolLabs.brief: Convert the TL-02 SQL into a real dbt project: staging models, a daily mart, data tests on every rule from TL-01/TL-02, and generated docs with lineage. Same logic, now versioned, tested, and documented.
steps: dbt init il26_chain --adapter duckdb; point profiles.yml at your analytics.duckdb file
Declare the source: raw orders CSV in models/sources.yml (source 'raw', table 'orders')
Write models/staging/stg_orders.sql: the TL-02 cleaning SELECT with {{ source('raw','orders') }}
Write models/marts/orders_daily.sql: the daily grain mart with {{ ref('stg_orders') }}
Add schema YAML: not_null + unique on order_id, relationships on customer_id, accepted_values on region/channel
Add singular tests: no_negative_amounts.sql and no_future_order_dates.sql (each must return 0 rows)
Run dbt build until green; then dbt docs generate and screenshot the lineage graph for your portfolio
toolLabs.deliverable: A green dbt build (models + all tests passing) and the generated docs site with lineage
toolLabs.checkpoint: dbt build exits 0 with all tests passing; dbt docs shows stg_orders -> orders_daily lineage; orders_daily totals match TL-02's mart exactly.

toolLabs.title: Tableau: Dashboard from the Modeled Data
toolLabs.brief: Connect Tableau to the dbt-built orders_daily mart (via the DuckDB export or CSV extract) and build the chain's reference dashboard: KPIs, trend, breakdowns. This dashboard is the baseline that TL-05 rebuilds and TL-06 cross-checks.
steps: Export the mart: COPY (SELECT * FROM clean.orders_daily) TO 'data/marts/orders_daily.csv' (HEADER) from DuckDB
Connect Tableau to orders_daily.csv; verify the date field is a Date and revenue is a Measure
Build a KPI sheet: total revenue, total orders, avg order value as BANs (big aggregate numbers)
Build a daily revenue trend line chart with a 7-day moving average (table calculation)
Build region and channel breakdowns (bar charts) with a region filter affecting all sheets
Assemble the dashboard: KPIs on top, trend middle, breakdowns bottom; title states the takeaway, not the topic
Publish to Tableau Public (or save the .twbx) and record the three KPI values for the TL-06 cross-check
toolLabs.deliverable: Published Tableau dashboard (link or .twbx) plus the three recorded KPI values
toolLabs.checkpoint: Dashboard KPIs match dbt's orders_daily totals (SELECT SUM(revenue), SUM(orders)); the region filter updates every sheet; title is a takeaway headline.

toolLabs.title: Power BI: Rebuild the Same Dashboard, Compare and Contrast
toolLabs.brief: Rebuild the identical dashboard in Power BI from the same orders_daily extract, then write the compare/contrast notes: DAX vs Tableau calculations, data modeling, and publishing. Same data, two tools, one honest comparison.
steps: Load orders_daily.csv into Power BI (Power Query); set date type and mark the date table
Write DAX measures: Total Revenue = SUM(orders_daily[revenue]), Total Orders, Avg Order Value = DIVIDE([Total Revenue],[Total Orders])
Rebuild the three KPI cards, the daily trend with 7-day moving average (DAX: AVERAGEX(DATESINPERIOD(...)))
Rebuild region/channel bar charts with a slicer; verify the slicer cross-filters like Tableau's filter
Write compare/contrast notes (min 300 words): calculations (DAX vs table calcs), modeling (star schema vs single extract), interactivity, publishing/sharing differences
Verify KPI parity: Power BI cards show EXACTLY the TL-04 recorded values — any difference is a bug to investigate, not a rounding note
toolLabs.deliverable: Power BI report (.pbix) plus written compare/contrast notes
toolLabs.checkpoint: All three KPIs match TL-04's recorded values to the cent; compare/contrast notes name at least one real workflow difference per tool (not just UI).

toolLabs.title: Excel/Sheets: Replicate 3 KPIs with Formulas and Pivots
toolLabs.brief: Prove the numbers are tool-independent: replicate total revenue, total orders, and avg order value in Excel/Sheets using formulas and a pivot table on the raw orders extract. The cross-tool reconciliation is the deliverable.
steps: Open data/clean/ecom_orders_clean.parquet's CSV export in Excel/Sheets (save a CSV copy for this lab)
Compute the 3 KPIs with formulas: =SUM(amount_range), =COUNTA(order_id_range), =AVERAGE(amount_range)
Build a pivot table: rows = region, values = Sum of amount and Count of order_id; add channel as a slicer
Build a second pivot: rows = order_date grouped by month, values = Sum of amount (the monthly trend)
Reconcile: Excel KPIs vs TL-04 Tableau values vs TL-05 Power BI values — all three must agree; document the reconciliation table
Write a 5-line note on what Excel made easy (ad-hoc pivots) vs hard (reproducibility, versioning) compared to the dbt+BI path
toolLabs.deliverable: Workbook (.xlsx or Sheet link) with KPI formulas, two pivots, and the 3-way reconciliation table
toolLabs.checkpoint: Reconciliation table shows Excel = Tableau = Power BI on all 3 KPIs; pivot monthly trend matches the dbt orders_daily monthly sums.

toolLabs.title: Streamlit: Ship the Interactive App
toolLabs.brief: Turn the chain's analysis into a clickable app: a Streamlit dashboard over the dbt mart with region/channel filters, KPIs, trend chart, and CSV download — structured per Module 45 (data.py / metrics.py / app.py) and deployed.
steps: Scaffold app/: data.py (cached DuckDB/CSV load of orders_daily + clean.orders), metrics.py (pure kpi() functions), app.py (layout only)
Sidebar controls: region multiselect, channel multiselect, date-range slider — all filters combine
Main canvas: 3 KPI metrics, daily revenue line chart, region bar chart, and an expandable raw-data table
Handle the empty state: zero matching rows shows 'No orders match these filters' guidance, never a blank page
Add st.download_button for the filtered data as CSV; verify the download matches the on-screen filters
Deploy (Streamlit Community Cloud or equivalent); README documents the question it answers, data source, refresh cadence, owner
Load-test manually: drag the date slider rapidly — the app must stay responsive (cache_data doing its job)
toolLabs.deliverable: Deployed Streamlit app URL plus the structured app/ source in git
toolLabs.checkpoint: App KPIs with no filters match the TL-04/05/06 reconciled values; filters update every visual; empty filters show the guidance message; download matches filters.

toolLabs.title: Capstone: Publish Everything and Embed in Your Portfolio
toolLabs.brief: The chain becomes a portfolio piece: a write-up page covering the question, methods, the 3-way tool reconciliation, and links to every artifact — Tableau, Power BI, Streamlit, dbt docs, and the git repo. This is the artifact hiring managers click.
steps: Write the case-study page: business question, dataset description (fictional), methods per lab (TL-01..TL-07 in one paragraph each)
Embed or link every artifact: Tableau Public dashboard, Power BI file/embedded report, Streamlit app, dbt docs lineage screenshot, git repo
Include the reconciliation table (TL-06) as the 'trust' section: same KPIs, three tools, identical numbers
Write the 'what I'd do with real data' section: scale notes (partitioning, incremental dbt, warehouse), contract terms you'd demand (Module 48), metric definitions you'd certify (Module 49)
Apply the Module 51 storytelling pass: headline states the finding, one message per section, honest charts with sources
Publish the page to your portfolio site; test every link; record the URL as the chain's final deliverable
toolLabs.deliverable: Published portfolio case-study page linking all chain artifacts
toolLabs.checkpoint: Every link on the page returns 200; the reconciliation table is present; the page states the dataset is fictional; a peer can follow the repo README and reproduce TL-01..TL-03.
